div.div: 1 وَسِخَ , aor. يَوْسَخُ (S, K) and يَاسَخُ and يَيْسَخُ, (K,) [the last two of which are irregular forms,] inf. n. وَسَخٌ; (L;) and ↓ إِتَّسَخَ and ↓ توسّخ (S, K) and ↓ استوسخ ; (K;) It (a garment, S, L, K, and the skin, L, or some other thing, Msb) was, or became, dirty, filthy, (S, L, K,) in consequence of its being seldom washed, (L,) or from want of care. (Msb.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
